four_concurrent_seeds.description: Four calling threads, each with its own store and engine set, released from a barrier; the cell reports the wall clock to the last commit. Two pool shapes were measured so that the overlap worker cannot be credited with the calling threads' own parallelism.
four_concurrent_seeds.note: overlap on is at or below overlap off in both shapes; no throughput was traded for the hidden digest

long_run.description: 40 overlap-on seeds in one process, 9 processes; resident set size is read after the first and the last round.
long_run.note: byte-identical resident set at start and end

interpretation: RuntimeBuilder::seed_digest_overlap(bool) runs a seed's content digest on the shared bounded Rayon pool concurrently with the seed encode; the digest bytes, validation ordering, error codes, and failure atomicity are identical to the serial path, and only wall-clock scheduling changes.
On this host the option hides 5.007 ms of a 4 MiB store-shape CPU seed (26.473 -> 21.466 ms p50, -18.9%), which is the pair quoted in docs/releases/v0.2.0.md.
The pre-release cell at a third of the sample count reproduces the same pair within 0.005 ms on both sides, so the figure is not an artifact of one campaign.
The Unicode-heavy row hides a comparable absolute amount (about 4.6-5.0 ms) of a much longer encode, which is what a fixed digest cost overlapped with a variable encode should look like.

Concurrency and long-run cells show no throughput loss and a byte-identical resident set, and the default remains off: the first overlap-on seed instantiates the global Rayon pool, which is a new footprint for a pure library embedding.
The GPU-routed counterpart of this option is measured separately in readings/rust_zero_copy_seed_w5.json (about 1.0 ms, -9.0%, on the RTX 5090 host).
